source_text: κηδεμονικωτάτην ἔνθεον ἐνέργειαν ἐκφαίνει οὑτωσί· 7.1ν ὅτι ζωοποιεῖ ὅτι ζωοποιεῖ, ὡς πνεῦμα ὑπάρχον τοῦ ζωογονοῦντος τὰ πάντα θεοῦ, κατὰ Παῦλον τὴν σάλπιγγα τῆς πίστεως, γράφοντα Ῥωμαίοις μέν· «ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν με ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου·» καὶ πάλιν· «ὁ ἐγείρας Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν, ζωοποιήσει καὶ τὰ θνητὰ ὑμῶν σώματα, διὰ τοῦ ἐνοικοῦντος αὐτοῦ πνεύματος ἐν ὑμῖν·» Κορινθίοις δέ· «οὐχ ὅτι ἱκανοί ἐσμεν ἀφ' ἑαυτῶν λογίσασθαί τι, ὡς ἐξ ἑαυτῶν· ἀλλ' ἡ ἱκανότης ἡμῶν ἐκ θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἱκάνωσεν ἡμᾶς διακόνους καινῆς διαθήκης, οὐ γράμματος, ἀλλὰ πνεύματος. τὸ γὰρ γράμμα ἀπο κτείνει, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωοποιεῖ.» γράμμα δὲ εἶπεν τὸν Μωσαϊκὸν νόμον, τὸν διαγορεύοντα· «ὀφθαλμὸν ἀντὶ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ ὀδόντα ἀντὶ ὀδόντος» καὶ ἀμυνόμενον τὸν ἀσυνέτως βιοτεύοντα· 68 ζωοποιὸν δὲ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ, τὸ μηκέτι ὑπὸ νόμον, ἀλλ' ὑπὸ χάριν ἡμᾶς ποιῆσαν καὶ παρεγγυῆσαν μὴ ἀποδοῦναι· «κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ», μᾶλλον δὲ ἀγαθὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ παρασχεῖν. «ἐάν», γὰρ φησίν, «πεινᾷ ὁ ἐχθρός σου, χόρτασον αὐτόν·» καὶ πάλιν τοῖς αὐτοῖς· «ἐγένετο ὁ πρῶτος Ἀδὰμ εἰς ψυχὴν ζῶσαν, ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀδὰμ εἰς πνεῦμα ζωοποιοῦν·» Γαλάταις δέ· «ὁ σπείρων εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα, ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος θερίσει ζωὴν αἰώνιον·» καὶ κατὰ Ἰωάννην λέγοντα ἀπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος· «τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστιν τὸ ζωοποιοῦν.» αὐτὸ δὴ τοῦτο δηλῶν Ἰεζεκιήλ, καὶ ὅτι σὺν τῷ θεῷ, ὡς πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ, τὴν ἀνάστασιν ποιήσει, προφητεύει· «τάδε λέγει κύριος τοῖς ὀστέοις τοῖς ξηροῖς τούτοις· ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ εἰσάγω εἰς ὑμᾶς πνεῦμα ζωῆς, καὶ δώσω ἐφ' ὑμᾶς νεῦρα, καὶ ἀνάξω ἐφ' ὑμᾶς σάρκας, καὶ ἐκτενῶ ἐφ' ὑμᾶς δέρμα, καὶ δώσω ἐφ' ὑμᾶς τὸ πνεῦμά μου, καὶ ζήσεσθε καὶ γνώσεσθε, ὅτι ἐγὼ κύριος.» ἡ οὖν οὐσιωδῶς ζωὴ καὶ ἡ ζωοποιὸς δύναμις οὔτ' ἀρχὴν οὔτε πέρας οὔτ' ἀλλοίωσιν ἔχει· τὸ δὲ τούτοις μὴ ὑποπῖπτον φύσει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ θεός ἐστιν, ἅτε δὴ καὶ τὰ κατ' ἐξαίρετον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς οἴκοθεν κεκτημένον. οὐδὲν γὰρ κτιστὸν ζωῆς αἴτιον εἶναι ἢ ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτῷ δεικνύναι δύναται· πάντα δὲ νεκρὰ τὰ τοῦ θεϊκοῦ πνεύματος ἐστερημένα· «ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ ζῶμεν καὶ κινούμεθα καὶ ἐσμέν,» ὡς ἔφασαν αἱ ἀποστολικαὶ πράξεις. καὶ γὰρ εἰ πάντα τὰ γινόμενα καὶ φθαρτά, τὰ δὲ φθειρόμενα στερεῖται ζωῆς ὑπομένοντα· πῶς ἂν ἄλλοις χαρίσαιτο ταῦτα, ὧν αὐτὰ γίνεται ἐνδεῆ; ζωοποιούμεθα δὴ οὖν ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, ὡς καὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ εἰπόντος· «ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ζωή.» 7.2ν ὅτι διὰ τὴν ταυτότητα τῆς θεότητος καὶ τὴν ἴσην ἐνέργειαν γέγραπται, ὡς ἤγειρεν τὸν ἑκουσίως δι' ἡμᾶς παθόντα σαρκὶ Χριστὸν ποτὲ πατὴρ, ποτὲ αὐτὸς ἑαυτόν, ποτὲ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα. καὶ κατὰ αἱρετικῆς ἐκθέσεως. ὅτι διὰ τὴν ταυτότητα τῆς θεότητος καὶ τὴν μίαν ἐνέργειαν λέγουσιν αἱ γραφαί, ὡς κατὰ τὴν τοῦ δούλου μορφὴν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἤγειρεν ποτὲ ὁ πατήρ, ποτὲ αὐτὸς ἑαυτόν, ποτὲ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα· οὑτωσὶ αἱ πράξεις· «τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ·» Ἰωάννης ἀπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος· «λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον, καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν. αὐτὸς δὲ ἔλεγεν περὶ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ·» καὶ πάλιν· «ἐγὼ τίθημι τὴν ψυχήν μου, ἵνα πάλιν λάβω αὐτήν. οὐδεὶς αἴρει αὐτὴν ἀπ' ἐμοῦ, ἀλλ' ἐγὼ τίθημι αὐτήν. ἐξουσίαν ἔχω θεῖναι αὐτήν, καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχω πάλιν λαβεῖν αὐτήν.» Πέτρος ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ ἐπιστολῇ· «Χριστὸς ἅπαξ περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀπέθανεν, δίκαιος ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων, ἵνα ἡμᾶς προσαγάγῃ τῷ θεῷ· θανατωθεὶς μὲν σαρκί, ζωοποιηθεὶς δὲ πνεύματι.» 7.3ν ὅτι δημιουργεῖ καὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγείρει. ἐν ταὐτῷ, ὅτι τὸ ἁγιάσαι δημιουργῆσαί ἐστιν καὶ ἀναγκαιότερον τοῦ δημιουργῆσαι. καὶ κατὰ αἱρετικῆς ἐκθέσεως. ὅτι δημιουργεῖ τὸ μέγα κτίσμα τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγείρει καὶ ζωοποιεῖ καὶ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἐπιστρέφει καὶ συγκαταρρυεῖσαν ταῖς ἀνθρωπίναις ἀνομίαις τὴν γῆν ἀνεκαίνισε
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: ... the oracles, having shown the divine and highest nature of the Holy Spirit, display as a match for it also the] most caring divine working, thus: 7.1ν [Chapter title:] That he gives life. That he gives life, as being Spirit of the God who engenders life in all things, according to Paul, the trumpet of the faith, writing to the Romans: 'for the law of the Spirit of the life in Christ Jesus freed me from the law of sin and of death'; and again: 'the one who raised Jesus Christ from the dead will give life also to your mortal bodies through his Spirit dwelling in you'; and to the Corinthians: 'not that we are sufficient from ourselves to reckon anything, as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God, who also made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant, not of letter but of Spirit. For the letter kills [the word split across a line], but the Spirit gives life.' And he called 'letter' the Mosaic law, the one prescribing: 'eye for eye and tooth for tooth', and punishing the one living without understanding; [page number 68, debris] and life-giving [he called] the Holy Spirit of God, the one having made us no longer under law but under grace, and having charged [us] not to give back 'evil for evil', but rather to furnish good for evil. For 'if', he says, 'your enemy hungers, feed him'; and again to the same: 'the first Adam came to be into a living soul, the last Adam into a life-giving spirit'; and to the Galatians: 'the one sowing into the Spirit will reap from the Spirit eternal life'; and according to John, saying from the Saviour: 'the Spirit is the one giving life.' Showing this very thing, and that together with God, as his Spirit, it will make the resurrection, Ezekiel prophesies: 'these things says the Lord to these dry bones: behold, I bring into you a spirit of life, and I will put upon you sinews, and I will bring up upon you flesh, and I will stretch out upon you skin, and I will put upon you my Spirit, and you will live and you will know that I am the Lord.' So the life that is in essence and the life-giving power has neither beginning nor end nor alteration; and that which does not fall under these is God by nature and in truth, inasmuch as it has acquired from within itself also the things that belong specially to God and Father. For nothing created can be cause of life or show life in itself; and all things deprived of the divine Spirit are dead: 'for in him we live and are moved and are,' as the apostolic Acts said. For indeed if all the things coming into being are also perishable, and the things perishing endure being deprived of life, how could they grant to others these things of which they themselves become in want? We are given life, then, by the Holy Spirit, as also by the one who said: 'I am the resurrection and the life.' 7.2ν [Chapter title:] That because of the sameness of the Godhead and the equal working it has been written that at one time the Father, at another he himself, at another the Holy Spirit raised Christ, the one who suffered willingly in flesh for our sake. And against a heretical exposition. That because of the sameness of the Godhead and the one working the Scriptures say that at one time the Father, at another he himself, at another the Holy Spirit raised Jesus Christ according to the form of the slave; thus the Acts: 'this one God raised on the third day'; John from the Saviour: 'destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it. And he was speaking about the temple of his body'; and again: 'I lay down my soul, that I may take it again. No one takes it from me, but I lay it down. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it again.' Peter in the first letter: 'Christ once died concerning sins on our behalf, just on behalf of unjust, that he might bring us to God, having been put to death in flesh, and having been made alive in Spirit.' 7.3ν [Chapter title:] That he creates and raises from the dead. In the same, that to sanctify is to create and more necessary than creating. And against a heretical exposition. That he creates the great creature, man, and raises from the dead and gives life and turns back into heaven, and the earth, having flowed down to ruin together with the human lawless deeds, renewed [continues in the next section: ... again, and the Holy Spirit warmed it back to life] ...
pass_b_english: …most caring divine working they display, in this way.

He gives life, since he is the Spirit of the God who brings all things to life. So says Paul, the trumpet of the faith, writing to the Romans: “For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and of death” (Romans 8:2); and again: “He who raised Jesus Christ from the dead will give life also to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you” (Romans 8:11). And to the Corinthians: “Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to reckon anything as coming from ourselves; our sufficiency is from God, who has also made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life” (2 Corinthians 3:5-6). By “the letter” he meant the law of Moses, which lays down “eye for eye and tooth for tooth” (Exodus 21:24) and punishes the one who lives without understanding. By the one who “gives life” he meant the Holy Spirit of God, who has put us no longer under law but under grace (Romans 6:14), and has charged us not to repay “evil for evil” (Romans 12:17), but rather to return good for evil. “If your enemy is hungry,” he says, “feed him” (Romans 12:20). And again, to the same church: “The first Adam became a living soul; the last Adam a life-giving spirit” (1 Corinthians 15:45). And to the Galatians: “He who sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap eternal life” (Galatians 6:8). So too John, speaking for the Saviour: “It is the Spirit that gives life” (John 6:63).

Ezekiel shows this very thing, and shows that the Spirit, being God’s own Spirit, will bring about the resurrection together with God, when he prophesies: “Thus says the Lord to these dry bones: Behold, I am bringing into you a spirit of life. I will put sinews upon you, bring up flesh upon you and stretch skin over you; I will put my Spirit upon you, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the Lord” (Ezekiel 37:5-6).

Life in its very being, the power that gives life, has neither beginning nor end nor change. And what is not subject to these things is God by nature and in truth, since it possesses of itself the very prerogatives of God the Father. For nothing created can be the cause of life or show life in itself; and all things deprived of the divine Spirit are dead. “For in him we live and move and are,” as the Acts of the Apostles said (Acts 17:28). Indeed, if all things that come into being are also perishable, and things that perish suffer the loss of life, how could they bestow on others what they themselves come to lack? We are given life, then, by the Holy Spirit, just as by him who said, “I am the resurrection and the life” (John 11:25).

That because the Godhead is the same and the working equal, it is written that Christ, who willingly suffered in the flesh for us, was raised at one time by the Father, at another by himself, at another by the Holy Spirit. And against a heretical statement of faith.

Because the Godhead is the same and its working one, the Scriptures say that Jesus Christ, in the form of the servant, was raised at one time by the Father, at another by himself, at another by the Holy Spirit. So the Acts: “This man God raised on the third day” (Acts 10:40). John, speaking for the Saviour: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up” (John 2:19). “But he was speaking of the temple of his body” (John 2:21). And again: “I lay down my life, that I may take it again. No one takes it from me, but I lay it down. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it again” (John 10:17-18). Peter in his first letter: “Christ died once for sins on our behalf, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring us to God, put to death in the flesh but made alive in the Spirit” (1 Peter 3:18).
That he creates and raises from the dead. With this, that to sanctify is to create, and is more needful than creating. And against a heretical statement of faith.

That he creates man, the great creature, raises him from the dead, gives him life and turns him back toward heaven; and that the earth, which had been swept down to ruin together with the lawless deeds of men, he renewed …

choices.issue: Garbled draft, dropped chapter title, wrong references
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u17): retranslated. The old English opened with 'The divine energy does not manifest itself in such a way', dropped the chapter title 7.1 ('That he gives life'), rendered παρεγγυῆσαν as 'guaranteed not to fail', νεῦρα as 'nerves', garbled the argument that life in its very being is God ('do not let this fall to these by nature', 'For which is it, even as those things...are possessed by inheritance'), read οὑτωσὶ αἱ πράξεις as 'but the actions are not so', ran the 7.2 title into its body, dropped 'willingly', rendered δι' ἡμᾶς as 'through us', and made 'the great creation' the subject of 7.3. References: (Ezekiel 37:12-14) -> (Ezekiel 37:5-6), as the reader report says; (2 Corinthians 3:6) -> (2 Corinthians 3:5-6); (John 2:19-21) split into (John 2:19) and (John 2:21), since verse 20 is not quoted; (Romans 12:20), (Romans 12:17) and (Romans 6:14) added. All checked against the KJV text.

choices.english: …most caring divine working they display, in this way.
choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence; the previous section ends 'the oracles ... also, as its equal, the …'. ἐκφαίνει is singular with the neuter plural τὰ λόγια, hence 'they display'. Only the words this section holds are translated.

choices.english: That he gives life. / He gives life
choices.why: The first is the chapter title 7.1, set as its own paragraph; the second opens the body. The printed '7.1' is an edition number and is dropped.
'According to Paul' introduces the proofs; a new English sentence keeps the period readable.

choices.english: By the one who “gives life” he meant the Holy Spirit
choices.why: Parallel to γράμμα δὲ εἶπεν; εἶπεν is understood from the previous clause.

choices.english: has charged us not to repay

choices.why: The last letter named is to the Corinthians, and 1 Corinthians 15:45 follows; 'church' is the natural English for 'the same [people]' and adds no claim.
As in Ezekiel 37:6; 'nerves' was a false friend.

choices.term: ἡ οὖν οὐσιωδῶς ζωὴ καὶ ἡ ζωοποιὸς δύναμις ... ἔχει
choices.english: Life in its very being, the power that gives life, has
choices.why: The two phrases name one thing (singular verb); 'essential life' would read as a technical term.

choices.term: τὰ κατ' ἐξαίρετον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς οἴκοθεν κεκτημένον
choices.english: it possesses of itself the very prerogatives of God the Father
choices.why: κατ' ἐξαίρετον = 'specially, as a prerogative'; οἴκοθεν = from within, not received from outside. The old 'possessed by inheritance' had no ground.
αἱ πράξεις is the book of Acts, quoted next (Acts 10:40); there is no negative.

choices.english: in the form of the servant
choices.why: Echoes Philippians 2:7; δοῦλος rendered 'servant' as the familiar phrase.
In John 10:17 ψυχή is the life laid down.

choices.english: And against a heretical statement of faith.
choices.why: ἔκθεσις is a written exposition or creed; part of the chapter titles 7.2 and 7.3.
'In the same [chapter]': the title adds a second theme to the same chapter.

choices.term: ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγείρει καὶ ζωοποιεῖ καὶ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἐπιστρέφει
choices.english: raises him from the dead, gives him life and turns him back toward heaven
choices.why: The verbs share the object τὸν ἄνθρωπον; 'him' is ordinary English, not bracketed.

choices.term: συγκαταρρυεῖσαν ταῖς ἀνθρωπίναις ἀνομίαις τὴν γῆν ἀνεκαίνισε
choices.english: the earth, which had been swept down to ruin together with the lawless deeds of men, he renewed …
choices.why: The section ends mid-sentence; the next section holds πάλιν καὶ ἀνέθαλψε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ('again, and warmed it back to life, the Holy Spirit'). Only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'.
ἀπο κτείνει is one word split across a printed line; 68 is a printed page number, skipped.
